raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`--quantization-param-path` loads per-layer KV cache scales from a JSON file through the models' `load_kv_cache_scales` (13 model files, including Llama, Qwen2 and Qwen3). They assign a Python float to `attn.k_scale` / `attn.v_scale` and leave `k_scale_float` / `v_scale_float` as None. The attention backends expect what `BaseKVCacheMethod` stores for checkpoint scales: `k_scale` as a device tensor and `k_scale_float` as its host value. So on main, a server with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --quantization-param-path <json>` fails during startup. The aiter backend fails in `reshape_and_cache_flash`:

```
ValueError: Unsupported ptr type triton.language.float32 in `tl.load`
```

and `--attention-backend triton` fails in `decode_attention_fwd`:

```
TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for *: 'float' and 'NoneType'
```

#37446 converts the scales for Qwen3.5 only and keeps the tensors on CPU, where the aiter and FA3 kernels cannot read them.

## Modifications

- `load_model_utils.load_kv_cache_scales`, the only caller of the models' loaders, now runs `_kv_cache_scales_to_tensors` after them: every `RadixAttention` whose scale is a float gets a 0-dim float32 tensor on the runner's device, and the float is kept in `k_scale_float` / `v_scale_float`. The model loaders are unchanged.
- `ModelRunner` passes `device=self.device`.
- New CPU test `test/registered/unit/model_executor/model_runner_components/test_load_kv_cache_scales.py` (`base-a-test-cpu`) checks the tensor, its host copy, and that a layer without a loaded scale is left as None. On main, after `load_kv_cache_scales` the layer still holds `k_scale = 0.25` as a float and `k_scale_float = None`.

## Accuracy Tests

MI355X (gfx950), image `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.22-rocm10-mi35x-20261025` (torch 2.11.0+rocm10, aiter `285579b6`), CUDA graphs on, KV cache `fp8_e4m3`. Llama runs use `meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct` with the repo's `test/manual/quant/kv_cache_scales_llama3_8b.json` (per-layer scales 0.04 to 0.18) and `python -m sglang.test.run_eval --eval-name gsm8k --num-examples 1319 --max-tokens 4096` (chat API, greedy). "x0.01" is the same JSON with every scale multiplied by 0.01: K/V then overflow the e4m3 range unless the loaded scale is actually applied, so it shows whether the kernels read the JSON scales.

**main `b960aa903a`, TP1.** On main both servers with the JSON fail to start with the errors above (aiter reports the `ValueError` inside a `CompilationError`).

| Attention backend | `--quantization-param-path` | main | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| aiter | none | 0.8166 | 0.8067 |
| aiter | `kv_cache_scales_llama3_8b.json` | fails to start | 0.8090 |
| aiter | same JSON x0.01 | — | 0.0046 |
| triton | none | — | 0.8067 |
| triton | `kv_cache_scales_llama3_8b.json` | fails to start | 0.8067 |
| triton | same JSON x0.01 | — | 0.0076 |

**More paths, this PR on main `b85d6a8893`.**

| Model, backend, TP | Calibrated JSON | All-1.0 JSON | No JSON | JSON x0.01 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Llama-3.1-8B, aiter (default decode), TP1 | 0.8105 / 0.8105 / 0.8044 | 0.8097 | 0.8029 | 0.0068 |
| Llama-3.1-8B, aiter unified-attention decode (`SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1`, `--page-size 16`), TP1 | 0.8128 | — | — | 0.0068 |
| Llama-3.1-8B, triton, TP1 | 0.8037 | — | 0.7968 | 0.0053 |
| Llama-3.1-8B, aiter, TP2 | 0.7877 / 0.8044 / 0.8044 | 0.8006 | 0.7983 | 0.0068 |
| Llama-3.1-8B, triton, TP2 | 0.8067 | — | — | 0.0053 |
| Qwen3-8B (qwen3 loader), aiter, TP1 | 0.892 / 0.889 / 0.886 / 0.886 | 0.901 / 0.898 / 0.897 | 0.906 / 0.897 / 0.901 / 0.898 | 0.005 |

Qwen3-8B uses 5-shot completion GSM8K (`python -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --num-questions 1319`), because the chat API makes Qwen3 think at length. Its JSON sets 0.05 for every layer (not calibrated), which caps K/V at 0.05 x 448 = 22.4; that file costs about 1.3 points, while the all-1.0 JSON matches the run without one, so the loading path itself does not change accuracy.

With calibrated scales every path scores within the run-to-run spread of the fp8 cache without scales, and scaling them by 0.01 breaks every path, so the loaded scales reach the kernels on aiter (both decode paths), triton, TP1 and TP2.

At TP>1 the JSON must give scales for every TP rank. The repo's `kv_cache_scales_llama3_8b.json` only has rank 0, so at TP2 the schema validation fails and `kv_cache_scales_loader` logs an error and falls back to 1.0 while the server starts normally (behavior on main, unchanged by this PR). The TP2 rows above use the same scales copied to ranks 0 and 1.

The JSON schema defines e4m3fn scales, while gfx942 stores the fp8 KV cache as e4m3fnuz (max 240); `BaseKVCacheMethod` doubles checkpoint scales there. On MI325X (gfx942), torch 2.11.0+rocm10.0.0, aiter `285579b62`, main `cb55d77d37` with this patch, doubling the JSON scales makes no measurable difference, so this PR loads them as given:

| Attention backend | JSON as given | JSON scales x2 |
|---|---|---|
| aiter | 0.8113 / 0.8158 | 0.8151 / 0.8196 |
| triton | 0.8166 | 0.8158 |

For reference on the same machine: aiter fp8 KV without JSON 0.8227, bf16 KV 0.8326.

Not tested: NVIDIA backends (FA3, FlashInfer). They already read checkpoint KV scales stored as a device tensor plus host float, which is the form this PR now gives JSON scales too.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The conversion runs once at model load; nothing changes in the forward pass. Measured on MI355X, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, aiter, TP1, this PR, `python -m sglang.bench_serving --dataset-name random-ids --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 512 --random-range-ratio 1.0 --num-prompts 256 --max-concurrency 32`, two runs each:

| KV cache scales | Output throughput (tok/s) | Median TPOT (ms) |
|---|---|---|
| `kv_cache_scales_llama3_8b.json` | 4512 / 4971 | 6.08 / 6.08 |
| none | 4513 / 5020 | 6.09 / 6.09 |

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

 )

 from sglang.srt.model_loader.remote_instance_weight_loader_utils import (

-def load_kv_cache_scales(*, model, kv_cache_dtype: str) -> None:
+def _kv_cache_scales_to_tensors(model, device: str) -> None:
+    """The models' ``load_kv_cache_scales`` assign float scales, while attention
+    backends read a device tensor plus its host copy, the way
+    ``BaseKVCacheMethod`` stores checkpoint scales."""
+    for module in model.modules():
+        if not isinstance(module, RadixAttention):
+            continue
+        for name in ("k_scale", "v_scale"):
+            scale = getattr(module, name)
+            if isinstance(scale, float):
+                setattr(module, f"{name}_float", scale)
+                setattr(
+                    module,
+                    name,
+                    torch.tensor(scale, dtype=torch.float32, device=device),
+                )
+
+
+def load_kv_cache_scales(*, model, kv_cache_dtype: str, device: str) -> None:
     """``kv_cache_dtype`` is the caller's resolved value. Required rather than
     defaulted: a fallback to ``server_args`` would be a hidden global read for
     any future caller that forgets to pass one."""
@@ -130,6 +149,7 @@ def load_kv_cache_scales(*, model, kv_cache_dtype: str) -> None:

             if callable(getattr(model, "load_kv_cache_scales", None)):
                 model.load_kv_cache_scales(get_model().quantization_param_path)
+                _kv_cache_scales_to_tensors(model, device)

@@ -0,0 +1,61 @@
+"""--quantization-param-path KV scales are stored the way checkpoint KV scales are."""
+
+import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.layers.radix_attention import RadixAttention
+from sglang.srt.model_executor.model_runner_components import load_model_utils
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+class _Model(torch.nn.Module):
+    """Assigns float scales the way the models' ``load_kv_cache_scales`` do."""
+
+    def __init__(self, scales):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.attn = torch.nn.ModuleList(
+            RadixAttention(
+                num_heads=2, head_dim=8, scaling=1.0, num_kv_heads=1, layer_id=i
+            )
+            for i in range(len(scales))
+        )
+        self.scales = scales
+
+    def load_kv_cache_scales(self, _path):
+        for attn, scale in zip(self.attn, self.scales):
+            if scale is not None:
+                attn.k_scale = attn.v_scale = scale
+
+
+class TestLoadKvCacheScales(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_float_scales_become_device_tensors_with_host_copies(self):
+        model = _Model([0.25, None])
+        with patch.object(
+            load_model_utils,
+            "get_model",
+            return_value=SimpleNamespace(quantization_param_path="scales.json"),
+        ):
+            load_model_utils.load_kv_cache_scales(
+                model=model, kv_cache_dtype="fp8_e4m3", device="cpu"
+            )
+
+        loaded, untouched = model.attn
+        for name in ("k_scale", "v_scale"):
+            scale = getattr(loaded, name)
+            self.assertIsInstance(scale, torch.Tensor)
+            self.assertEqual(scale.dtype, torch.float32)
+            self.assertEqual(scale.shape, torch.Size([]))
+            self.assertEqual(scale.device, torch.device("cpu"))
+            self.assertEqual(scale.item(), 0.25)
+            self.assertEqual(getattr(loaded, f"{name}_float"), 0.25)
+            self.assertIsNone(getattr(untouched, name))
+            self.assertIsNone(getattr(untouched, f"{name}_float"))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

This PR only changes behavior when `kv_cache_dtype == "fp8_e4m3"` and a `quantization_param_path` is given, so the code path is never reached there. The same test also failed on main's scheduled run (https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41542824410, speed 241.5 / 239.6), so it looks like a flaky perf threshold.

Follow-up: the root cause is that this run tests the merge with main `1ced9a9eb0`, before #47989 relaxed this threshold from 250 to 200. A fresh CI run on current main should pass. I'm rebasing this PR onto the latest main.
[BBuf Review Agent] @zengleixin-amd The failing test doesn't pass a quantization param path, so it skips the scale conversion added here. Agreed this failure is unrelated to the PR.
[BBuf Review Agent] @zengleixin-amd Confirmed this head already includes #47989 and the threshold is now 200. That addresses the reported throughput failure; marking it unrelated.
